podcast-dannyjones-7G0ql9EDdxM:
Former ecstasy kingpin Shaun Attwood explains stock market scams to Danny Jones in this episode. Attwood, an Englishman who ran a huge ecstasy ring in Arizona, served prison time and became a writer and speaker. Here he shares a fraudster's playbook for rigging the markets.

Attwood walks through pump-and-dump schemes and how promoters lure small investors in. He compares the drug game's hustle with the stock game's, and finds them cousins. Jones asks how a normal saver can spot the trap. Wary and fascinated listeners learn that crime pays, then costs, in both of Attwood's worlds.
podcast-joerogan-PJ2YwE0R-xM:
UFO witnesses Lenval Logan and Jason Sands join the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2264. Both men served in the military and say they encountered things their training could not explain. Their testimony has been part of the recent wave of insider accounts reaching the public.

They tell Rogan what they saw, in sequence, and how their services reacted when they spoke up. Rogan asks what they make of each other's stories and of the officials now hinting at hidden programs. The episode adds two first-hand voices to the disclosure record, valuable whether a listener ends up convinced or not.
podcast-tuckercarlson-KAKGW2SxSxM:
Entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy joins Tucker Carlson just a day after Trump's sweeping win. Trump took the popular vote, the electoral vote, and both houses. Carlson marvels at the scale of the sweep.

Ramaswamy says the win was a rejection of the modern left. He argues the left's offer provoked a rebellion in reply. The title asks what the win means for the federal bureaucracy. Ramaswamy lays out plans to shrink and reshape it. The episode captures victory-hour thinking from a young ally with big reform plans. The mood is triumph mixed with a work list.
podcast-tuckercarlson-claOs_1LjXM:
Comedian and commentator Dave Smith joins Tucker Carlson for a talk on feuds inside the right. The title names his debate with Douglas Murray, the woke right label, and the moment Smith says he found God. Smith speaks as a libertarian voice.

Smith tells how the debate with Murray went and why the woke right tag angers him. He argues the right is split over war, Israel, and free speech. Carlson draws out his late turn toward faith. Listeners get a clear map of one loud fight on the right, from a man in the middle of it.
